executive_assessment.text: Named Wielkopolska water-retention projects and Bydgoszcz/Gdańsk/Katowice cases give local adaptation detail; the national 2025 climate summary and preliminary 2024 flood counts retain their distinct scopes and vintages.
Eastern Poland project targeting and staffing constraints add institutional depth. Funding, legal deadlines and policy judgments are not verified uptake, completion or climate-conflict evidence.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated not stated reports: The Ministry identifies Wielkopolska among Poland's most drought-affected regions, citing low rainfall, hydrology, intensive farming, low forest cover and a water balance worsening since the early 2000 s.

Source dated not stated reports: The Ministry says rising temperatures, long dry spells and snowless winters worsen Wielkopolska's water balance; open-pit mining and intensive farming further deepen drought problems.

Source dated not stated reports: On 2 April 2026, the Ministry and regional partners signed a water-retention and water-security letter, joining administration, science and public bodies around catchment-scale planning.

Source dated not stated reports: The Ministry lists lake protection in Powidz Landscape Park, Ślesiński Canal modernization, Gniezno Lakeland water-resource restoration and hydrological restoration in the Warcica basin as in implementation.
Source dated 2024 reports: Bydgoszcz's project began in 2017: 14 km new and about 90 km renovated storm sewers, six reservoirs and 22 treatment plants; target capture was about 37,000 m³.

Source dated 2024 reports: Gdańsk invested PLN 380m in drainage and flood infrastructure during 2001–2015; storage rose over fivefold, while losses in two heavy-rain events fell from PLN 130m (2001) to PLN 10m (2016).

Source dated 2024 reports: The report describes Katowice's post-industrial adaptation features, including a green roof and planted public spaces; Bogucki Park's revitalization included a planned underground rainwater reservoir.
Source dated 2024-09-21 reports: Preliminary reports counted 11,502 damaged residential buildings, 6,033 farm buildings and 724 public buildings; Lower Silesia alone reported damage to 54 schools.
Source dated not stated reports: The project targets medium cities and spa municipalities in Podkarpackie, Lubelskie, Świętokrzyskie, Podlaskie, Warmian-Masurian and part of Mazowieckie.

known_gaps.text: No direct, country-specific primary source-stated climate-to-FCV or FCV-to-adaptation pathway was found in the completed searches; this is an evidence-search gap, not evidence that no such relationship exists.
The Statistics Poland 2024 flood report could not be directly opened; search-indexed claims about local-government losses and affected population were excluded.
The 2025 IMGW report PDF exceeded the available fetch limit; its claims are limited to the directly read publisher landing-page summary.
The World Bank urban case study summarizes selected municipal projects; source adaptation plans and independent project evaluations were not inspected.
The 21 September 2024 flood impact counts are explicitly preliminary government figures, not a final damage assessment.
National climatic/resource indicators are not treated as local vulnerability rankings. Eastern Poland institutional capacity is not an FCV classification.
No complete supported climate–FCV chain is assembled; historic flood impacts, municipal adaptation and implementation constraints remain distinct from violence/conflict claims.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
